land.text: western Moghulistan, Mahmud Khan's part: 'ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent'; the Cliopatria 1491 Moghulistan shape minus its 1492 shape

predecessors.note: The same khanate: the Moghulistan page calls it the 'Eastern Chagatai Khanate' and Cliopatria shares Wikidata Q1191125. The page dates the division of Yunus Khan's realm to 1487 (Mahmud 1487-1508 at Tashkent, Ahmad Alaq 1487-1503 at Turpan); Cliopatria and the moghulistan dossier split it in 1492.

land.text: the Zhetysu of the Eastern Chagatai shape, which Cliopatria re-absorbs into its Moghulistan row in 1512

successors.note: Bridging: the Moghulistan page says the Kyrgyz 'had effectively driven out the Moghuls' by 1510-11 and names no heir to the land. The moghulistan dossier records the same 1512 joining at confidence 1.

capitals.name: Tashkent
capitals.note: Mahmud Khan 'ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent'; Tashkent was 'seized by the Uzbeks' in 1503. The pages name no seat for 1504-1511.

correction.text: western Moghulistan: the Cliopatria Eastern Chagatai shape (Zhetysu and the Issyk-Kul steppe by its outline) with Tashkent, 'ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent'

keyframe_review.note: 303,000 km2 (71.6-81.1 E, 38.7-46.5 N): the Zhetysu, Issyk-Kul and the western Tian Shan by outline; the Moghulistan page gives no area (its infobox map shows the territory in 1490) and does not name Zhetysu. The shape leaves out Tashkent, where the page puts Mahmud Khan (reign 1487-1508) and which he held until the Uzbeks seized it in 1503; Cliopatria draws Tashkent as Kazakh Khanate land in these years (132 of the 149 cells of a 120 km disk) and as Shaybanid from 1502. Tashkent is added for 1492-1502.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid from 1503 (Tashkent and the Fergana edge lost to the Uzbeks in 1503); Cliopatria's 1502 step is a year early

keyframe_review.note: 284,804 km2 for 1502-06: Cliopatria drops 59 cells (14,900 km2 at 71.6-75.7 E, 40.5-43.1 N, the Fergana and Naryn edge; 58 of them become Shaybanid) in 1502. The Moghulistan page dates the loss to 1503: 'Ahmad Alaq traveled west to help Mahmud against Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks. The brothers were defeated and captured, and Tashkent was seized by the Uzbeks.' So the shape holds, with Tashkent, to 1502 and without it from 1503.

284,804 km2, unchanged for 1507-11. Mahmud's reign ends in 1508 (executed by Shaybani, undated) and 'by 1510-11 ... the Kyrgyz had effectively driven out the Moghuls' from the Tian Shan, which fits the end of the row in 1511; nothing on the pages says who held the land in 1504-1509. unverified: page budget.

region.text: western Moghulistan: the Cliopatria Eastern Chagatai shape (Zhetysu and the Issyk-Kul steppe by its outline) with Tashkent, 'ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent'

ledger.note: 1492: the western Moghuls under Mahmud Khan hold Tashkent and the Zhetysu as a khanate of their own. Confidence 1 for the year, which is Cliopatria's (its Moghulistan row loses this shape in 1492): the Moghulistan page lists Yunus Khan 1462-1487, Ahmad Alaq 1487-1503 ('ruled eastern Moghulistan or Turpan Khanate from Turpan') and 'Mahmud Khan ... 1487-1508' as 'ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent', so the division is the page's 1487. The moghulistan dossier keeps the combined khanate to 1491; move both to 1487 if the rows are merged.

region.text: Tashkent, 'seized by the Uzbeks', and the Fergana-Naryn edge (59 cells) that Cliopatria hands to the Shaybanids in 1502

ledger.note: 1503: Tashkent falls to Shaybani. 'In 1503 Ahmad Alaq traveled west to help Mahmud against Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks. The brothers were defeated and captured, and Tashkent was seized by the Uzbeks'; the Shaybani page lists the Battle of Akhsi in 1503 without detail. The 59-cell edge is Cliopatria's step of 1502.

region.text: the Zhetysu of the Eastern Chagatai shape

ledger.note: 1511: the Moghuls are gone from the Tian Shan. 'By 1510-11, the Kyrgyz had effectively driven out the Moghuls'; Mahmud's reign ended in 1508 (page's reign dates); Shaybani executed him after he submitted, in a year the page does not give. Cliopatria re-absorbs the shape into its Moghulistan row in 1512, which the page does not say; the land's holder in 1512 is the Kyrgyz by the page and Moghulistan by Cliopatria.

wars.name: Shaybani's war against Mahmud Khan and Ahmad Alaq
wars.outcome: The brothers Mahmud and Ahmad Alaq were defeated and captured by Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks and Tashkent was seized; Mahmud later submitted to Shaybani, who executed him (the page ends his reign in 1508 and gives no year for the execution).
wars.note: Shaybani page: the Battle of Akhsi in 1503, with no detail and no mention of Ahmad Alaq; earlier (1488) Shaybani had met Mahmud and the Battle of the Chirciq River gave 'decisive victory for Moghulistan' over Ahmed Mirza.

wars.name: Kyrgyz expulsion of the Moghuls

zones.text: the western Tian Shan and Zhetysu

wars.outcome: By 1510-11 the Kyrgyz 'had effectively driven out the Moghuls' from the Tian Shan.
wars.note: The page gives no battle or month; a different 'Kyrgyz gained ground in the Tian Shan' narrative is in the moghulistan dossier.

certainty.note: Steppe and mountain frontiers; the pages give no boundary of the khanate at all, and the shape is Cliopatria's outline.

notes:
Same state as Moghulistan or not. The Moghulistan page calls the whole khanate 'Eastern Chagatai Khanate' and Cliopatria gives Moghulistan, Eastern Chagatai Khanate, Eastern Moghulistan and Western Moghulistan one Wikidata id (Q1191125). The rows are different parts of one khanate cut in halves by Cliopatria (the moghulistan dossier of ia-02-d says the same): this row is the western part under Mahmud Khan (the Zhetysu and, on the page, Tashkent) for 1492-1511. I wrote it as its own dossier because the moghulistan dossier already exists and the 1519 rows belong to ia-03; the orchestrator may merge all four into the moghulistan dossier.
Dates: the page puts the division in 1487 (Mahmud 1487-1508, Ahmad Alaq 1487-1503) while Cliopatria and the moghulistan dossier split in 1492; I follow 1492 so that the two dossiers do not claim the Zhetysu together, and enter the year at confidence 1. Tashkent: the page has Mahmud there from 1487 to 1503; Cliopatria gives it to the Kazakh Khanate (1483-1501) and the Shaybanids (1502-), so the Kazakh dossier (ia-03) should be checked for the same land. Before the state's start the Shaybani page has (1488) Shaybani's oppression of the Kazakhs lead to a war in which 'Moghulistan lost'; no land is named and the Kazakh dossier should settle Tashkent. Unsettled: who held the Zhetysu in 1504-1509 (page silent), Mahmud's execution year (1508 is the end of his reign, no year for the execution), the Kazakh war's end, and the Kyrgyz heir. Pages: 2 of 2 (Moghulistan, Muhammad Shaybani). No Seshat page exists for the row. No rulers written.
